title: Candida tropicalis filamentation assay with fluconazole
author: Laboratorio de Microbiología Mr JORGE ENRIQUE PEREZ CARDENAS
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bxh8pj9w
materials: Fluconazole preparation Weigh 6.4 mg of Fluconazole (Cat Sigma: F8929) Dissolve in 1 ml of Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) aliquot and freeze at -80°C

CULTURE OF C. tropicalis TO HARVEST YEAST FOR TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS Obtain a Fluconazole Strain and a certificate strain (ATCC750) Establish the susceptibility grade of both strains Culture both strains with filamentation (RPMI+SFB) and Non-filamentation (RPMI+NAC) media, using Fluconazole at subinhibitory concentrations Incubate at 35°C by 24 hrs with constant agitation (200 rpm) Check the growth degree and filamentation degree Harvest the colonies with a sterile Pasteur pipet Centrifuge at high speed Extract the supernatant Add RNA later (Sigma Aldrich Ref0901) Freeze at -80°C until the RNA extraction

steps.title: Prepare RPMI medium with NAC
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g RPMI 1640, 35 g MOPS, and 20 g N‑acetyl‑glucosamine in 500 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 7.0, bring the final volume to 1000 mL, and sterilize the solution by filtration. This medium (RPMI+NAC) inhibits filamentation.

steps.title: Prepare RPMI medium with SFB
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g RPMI 1640, 35 g MOPS, and 20 g glucose in 500 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 7.0, bring the final volume to 1000 mL, filter‑sterilize, then add 10 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum. This medium (RPMI+SFB) promotes filamentation.

steps.title: Grow and standardize Candida inoculum
steps.instruction: Streak Candida tropicalis on Potato dextrose agar or inoculate liquid Sabouraud broth and incubate 24 h at 35 °C. Pick one or two colonies, suspend them in sterile saline, vortex until homogeneous, and adjust the turbidity to a 0.5 McFarland standard (≈1 × 10⁶–5 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Make inoculum dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the standardized suspension 1:100 in the appropriate medium (RPMI+NAC or RPMI+SFB) and vortex for 15 seconds. From this 1:100 dilution, perform a further 1:20 dilution to obtain a final yeast concentration of 5 × 10²–3 × 10³ CFU per well.

steps.title: Prepare fluconazole stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare fluconazole working solutions in DMSO at the following concentrations: 6400, 3200, 1600, 800, 400, 200, 100, 50, 25, and 12.5 µg mL⁻¹. These will be used to generate the final test concentrations.

steps.title: Set up MIC plate with RPMI+NAC
steps.instruction: Using a sterile 24‑well plate, add 90 µL RPMI+NAC to each well. Then add 10 µL of the appropriate fluconazole working solution to achieve final drug concentrations of 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.25, and 0.125 µg mL⁻¹ (high‑range series from 6400‑200 µg mL⁻¹ stocks and low‑range series from 100‑12.5 µg mL⁻¹ stocks). Add 10 µL DMSO to the positive‑control (C+) and negative‑control (C‑) wells. Finally, add 900 µL of the 1:20 inoculum dilution to every well.

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL RPMI+NAC to each well
Add 10 µL fluconazole working solution for the desired concentration
Add 10 µL DMSO to control wells (C+ and C‑)
Add 900 µL 1:20 inoculum dilution to each well

steps.title: Set up MIC plate with RPMI+SFB
steps.instruction: Repeat the procedure of the previous step using RPMI+SFB instead of RPMI+NAC. Add 90 µL RPMI+SFB, 10 µL fluconazole working solution (same concentration series), 10 µL DMSO to control wells, and 900 µL inoculum to each well.

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL RPMI+SFB to each well
Add 10 µL fluconazole working solution for the desired concentration
Add 10 µL DMSO to control wells (C+ and C‑)
Add 900 µL 1:20 inoculum dilution to each well

steps.title: Incubate plates and assess growth
steps.instruction: Incubate both 24‑well plates at 35 °C for 24 h with constant agitation (~200 rpm). After incubation, examine each well with an inverted microscope, comparing growth to the positive and negative controls.

steps.title: Determine MIC and record filamentation
steps.instruction: Identify the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) as the lowest fluconazole concentration where ≥50 % inhibition of growth is observed relative to controls. Record the filamentation grade for each well.
